prompt: For $f(x) = x^2$, find the average rate of change from $x = 1$ to $x = 4$.
hint: Find the two heights first, then take rise over run.

hints.text: Find the two heights first, then take rise over run.
$f(1) = 1$ and $f(4) = 16$, so the rise is $16 - 1 = 15$ and the run is $4 - 1 = 3$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Draw the connecting line
steps: Plot (1, 1) and (4, 16) on the U-shaped graph of y = x².
Lay a ruler across those two points — that straight line is called a secant line.
Its slope, 15 over 3, is 5. Average rate of change is always the slope of the connecting line.

alternativeExplanations.title: Steeper and steeper
steps: From x = 1 to x = 2, the rise is 3 over a run of 1: rate 3.
From x = 2 to x = 3 the rate is 5, and from x = 3 to x = 4 it is 7.
The three rates average to (3 + 5 + 7) ÷ 3 = 5 — the same answer, and it shows the curve steepening as you go right.
